method: I did not write these rules and did not open tests/bench_1260.js, any review*_1260.json, or the 1.24.20 changelog/report. I read the source of AI_PUZZLE_TRACK, AI_WHEEL, AI_WHEEL_COLOURS and HEALTH_CHAT in both versions, wrote my own inputs, and worked out every expected answer by hand before running anything. Both versions were booted in Node + jsdom (the boot given in the brief) and each case was run on both and timed: TRACK through Lantern.aiTrack.run, wheels through Lantern.aiAct.build (the parts in plan.parts, and the colour of the first triangle of each wedge in shapes, checked against the colour's own hue within 35 degrees), bites through Lantern.healthLessons (key health_bites) and Lantern.healthNeed. Verdicts: right = the expected answer or one listed as also right; missed = a right input sent back as a problem (for rule 3 also: a wheel written as groups for a plain colour-wheel question left as written, as 1.24.19 did); spoiled = a right input answered silently wrong (rule 3: a block that is right as written for its question re-cut by hue; rule 5: a question that is not a bite to a person given the Bites lesson); mended-wrong = an input that should go back (ambiguous, two steps on a line, off the row) answered silently instead. Rule 5: every question is a right input (a person's own question); the expected field says whether it is a bite to a person. newIn_1_24_20 = the 1.24.20 verdict is worse than 1.24.19's. Beyond the hand cases: (1) a differential fuzz: gen.js writes TRACK scripts (rows of 3-7 people or cups; swaps, puts, passes, moves, shifts, reverses, adds, removes, swap contents, repeat counts) with places in many forms, and keeps its own simulator written from the puzzle's meaning (not from Lantern's code) as the oracle; 60,000 scripts were run on both versions, every silent wrong answer of 1.24.20 was looked at, and the families found were written as plain hand cases (T210-T239); (2) a word-soup fuzz: 8,000 random TRACK scripts, 8,000 random health questions and 2,700 random wheel blocks with random questions, for crashes and time; (3) hand-built worst cases for time (nesting to the depth limit, 100 times on a 290-character line, a 2,000-thing row with 300 lines). mostSerious: TRACK, a relation word before an ordinal is dropped (new in 1.24.20). place() now strips a leading word before any word in REL, and REL gained first..fifth, front of, on, next, beside, between; bareOf() also strips any one word before '<ordinal> from|to ...'. So 'behind the first person' reads as the first person, 'after the second' as the second, 'the person behind the second from the front' as the second from the front, 'before the second to last' as the second to last, 'behind the front of the queue' as the front. The same happens where a thing lands (spot): 'move Ed behind the second from the front', 'add Fay after the third from the left', 'insert Fay before the second to last', 'Fay joins behind the second from the front' all put the person one place off; and removals ('remove behind the front of the queue', 'the person behind the second from the front leaves') take out the wrong person. Silent wrong answers on right inputs: T210, T214-T226 (1.24.19 asked: a silent wrong answer where the old version asked), T211, T212, T227 (1.24.19 was right). 302 of the 334 silent wrong answers 1.24.20 gave in the 60,000-script fuzz are this family; the other 32 are 'behind <left of|N right of|in front of> X' (1.24.19 was wrong on most of those too; where a row name is in the phrase 1.24.19 was right, its !thing(s) guard is gone). The fuzz also showed it hiding behind later problems: 'remove behind third' removed the third person, and a later line then failed on the person who should still be there.

TRACK T09, a count on a two-step line (new): 'swap Red and Blue twice, then swap Red and Green' is now run as 'swap Red and Green' twice and gives the row unchanged, silently; 1.24.19 asked. Removing 'twice' leaves 'Blue,' with its comma, which no longer counts as a name, so the pair splits at the second 'and' and the one name left on each side is taken.

Wheel, a cut said in words on the fixed list (new): 'in one ... in the other', 'on one ... on the other', 'one for warm and one for cool', 'in two', 'in three', 'with two:', 'all ... in one and all ... in one', and 'Draw two colour wheels: one of primary colours and one of secondary colours' are all made of plain-list words (one, other, in, on, two, three, each, all, it), so the groups are re-cut into one hue-ordered wheel: W23, W24, W25, W26, W32, W60, W63, W64, W65, W66. The order and the painted colours of every split were right.

Bites, a scene or a thing that is not a person (new): the who-was-bitten reading only looks after the person, so a dream, story, film, game or poster said before ('I dreamt a snake bit me', 'In the film a shark bit a swimmer', 'On the poster, a dog bit a boy', 'In Minecraft a spider bit me', 'a snake bit a man in the story', 'the dog bit a boy in my dream'), 'them' meaning things ('I left my shoes out and my dog bit them', 'The dog bit them both, the cushions and the rug'), and 'him' meaning another animal of the same kind ('My dog fought another dog and the other dog bit him badly': beasts() counts kinds, so two dogs are one) now get the Bites lesson: N46-N56. 1.24.19 gave none.
